unit: one event per changelog item of 2025-03-26, 2025-06-18, 2025-11-25 and 2026-07-28 (quote: the item's first line)

kinds.added: a new mechanism, field or option
kinds.removed: a mechanism is dropped from the specification
kinds.replaced: a mechanism is dropped and a named successor takes its place
kinds.deprecated: still in the specification but scheduled for removal (or reclassified as Deprecated)
kinds.changed: an existing mechanism's behaviour, requirement level, value or shape changes
kinds.clarified: wording or guidance only, no normative change of behaviour
kinds.governance: process or governance, not the protocol

related_earlier: the earlier events whose mechanism this event removes, replaces, deprecates or changes, in whole or in part. A clarified event has no mechanism of its own and is never the earlier end of a link: a later event that ends what a clarification says is linked to the event whose mechanism the clarification clarifies. A catalog of relations between changelog items, NOT an oracle of stale answers: a link does not mean that every earlier statement about that mechanism became false (see mcp-spec-2026-07-28-stale-facts.json)

Remove protocol-level sessions and the `Mcp-Session-Id` header from the Streamable HTTP transport. List endpoints (`tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list`) no longer vary per-connection. Servers that need cross-call state use explicit, server-minted handles passed as ordinary tool arguments ([SEP-2567](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2567)).

Make MCP stateless: remove the `initialize`/`notifications/initialized` handshake. Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion`, `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`). Clients SHOULD identify themselves on each request (`io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo`), and servers SHOULD identify themselves in each result's `_meta` (`io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo`). Version mismatches return `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` ([SEP-2575](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2575)).

decision.quote: Every request now carries its protocol version and client capabilities in `_meta`
decision.why: Removing the handshake ends the lifecycle MUSTs and moves the negotiated protocol version from the HTTP header mechanism into `_meta`.

correction.why: the handshake is removed, but HTTP POST requests still carry the MCP-Protocol-Version header, now matched against the version in _meta

Clients MAY call it before any other request for up-front version selection, or use it as a backward-compatibility probe on STDIO ([SEP-2575](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2575)).

Replace the HTTP GET endpoint and `resources/subscribe`/`resources/unsubscribe` with `subscriptions/listen`: a single long-lived POST-response stream for opted-in server-to-client change notifications. Clients opt in to specific types (`toolsListChanged`, `promptsListChanged`, `resourcesListChanged`, `resourceSubscriptions`); the server acknowledges and tags notifications with `io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId`. Request-scoped notifications such as `notifications/progress` and `notifications/message` continue to flow on the response stream of the request they relate to, not the `subscriptions/listen` stream ([SEP-2575](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/modelcontextprotocol/pull/2575)).

events.quote: Multi Round-Trip Requests (MRTR) pattern introduced which replaces the previous approach of sending server-initiated requests, such as `roots/list`, `sampling/createMessage`, or `elicitation/create`. Servers return an `InputRequiredResult` (`resultType: "input_required"`) whose `inputRequests` field carries the requests for the additional information needed to process the request.
